claim: For every integer \(n\ge 2\), let \(D_n\) be the loopless digraph with central vertices \(c_i\) indexed by \(i\in\mathbb Z/(2n)\mathbb Z\), poles \(p_0,p_1\), central arcs \(c_i\to c_{i+1}\), and bidirected spokes between \(c_i\) and \(p_{i\bmod 2}\). For the non-regular integral path-homology convention of Chowdhury--Huntsman--Yutin, \(\widetilde H_1(D_n;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\). Thus the torsion subgroup is exactly \(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\) for every \(n\ge2\), proving the published alternating-pole torsion conjecture and determining the full first path homology.
integrity: The all-parameter theorem is proved algebraically. The finite verifier is only a regression check and is not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem uses the non-regular integral path-homology convention of the motivating source.
Only first path homology is determined; no higher path-homology or digraph-homotopy classification is claimed.
An obscure or unindexed independent proof cannot be absolutely excluded.
title: Exact first path homology of the alternating-pole torsion family
